easy: Easier than an even game; the best level for learning
standard: About an even game with two to four rivals; a little tougher with five
hard: About as strong as the app's rivals
method: Each cell is 360 games on seeds (block 200000) not used to tune the rules, played with v0.4.0 (rival tie-break). Lower means tougher rivals. In a perfectly even game the player would win 33% against two rivals, 25% against three, 20% against four and 17% against five.
strategy: **Strategy balance.** Chasing Domination cards is still the strongest simple approach: at Standard it wins 15–44% against 2–25% for spreading out or chasing majorities. A simple habit of taking Initiative whenever you are not first adds a few points (in an independent audit run, 30% against 25% at Standard). A self-tuned test player that fights hard for turn order and Domination spaces (checkpoint v3, re-tuned against these rules) does much better. In two held-out samples it beat the card-chaser at Hard by 30 and 35 points, against 25 to 28 points against the app's rivals; at Standard by 39 and 44 points. Without the rival tie-break its margin at Hard was about 51 points. If you play this way, choose Hard or Expert.
stalls: No test game stalled: every game reached a normal end. If the action display fills before every rival has placed, Planning simply ends and the extra pawns wait for the next turn.
